cases.exactVsDesignFamilyBoundary: Calling it a Roman dodecahedron is useful identification. Claiming one original purpose as fact is unsupported and must fail the ambiguity contract.

supportedValuationRange.limitations: No private-market valuation is appropriate from these images; title, provenance, cultural-property law, and museum status control any disposition.

minimumPracticalActionPlanElements: identify the holding institution and accession record

cases.provenanceAndVerifierNotes: Two independently created open-license photographs show the same large Lyon museum artifact, matched by punched circular decoration, face-hole geometry, and patina. The control deliberately distinguishes confident object-class recognition from unresolved historical function.

ambiguityContract.whyExactUnsupported: No surviving inscription, standardized context, or accepted scholarly consensus establishes the original function of Roman dodecahedra, and photographs cannot resolve it.
